text:
alice.m: heads-up — since ~03:00 UTC we've been seeing a creeping pile of Pending GPU pods in eu-west1. ~50 pods stuck in Pending with message 'waiting for lease' and kubelet logs show a bunch of cold-slot leases that never get re-bound. looks like latebind + warm-pool mismatch + some sticky lease state.

ben_p: saw the alert. any pattern on instance type / rack?

alice.m: mostly p4d-ish racks, 3 racks are reporting >10 pending each. BPF net metrics show a small conntrack spike around the same time. not sure if network flaps are preventing the lease handshake.

carla: can you paste an example of the pod event and the node lease log?

alice.m: sure — pod event: `FailedScheduling: 0/120 nodes are available: 120 0/GPUs match, waiting for lease`. node lease snippets: ```
I0302 03:02:11 lease_controller.go:212] lease renew failed: context deadline exceeded
I0302 03:02:12 lease_controller.go:250] mark node gpu-node-az3 as sticky-lease=abc123
I0302 03:02:15 kubelet: late-bind attempt timed out, leaving slot reserved
```

dinesh: that last line looks like our known 'sticky cold-slot' behavior when latebind timeout fires but the scheduler doesn't clear the reservation. we've seen it when daemonset restarts interrupt the renew path.

sre-oncall: ops-bot posted related alerts at 03:05 for conntrack high-water on gw-eu-west1c, could be correlated.

ops-bot: ALERT: conntrack count > 80% on gw-eu-west1c (03:05 UTC) — remediation: scale NAT gateway / rotate nodes.

ben_p: if reservations are sticky we should force a short descheduler run to unreserve orphaned leases and let pending pods bind. low-risk window?

carla: agree. run descheduler with `RemoveOrphanedLeases` + 5m dry-run first. also propose rolling restart of lease-controller on the 3 affected racks.

alice.m: i'll queue the descheduler dry-run now and post results. if dry-run shows >20 orphaned leases -> promote to real run.

dinesh: also open a follow-up to increase latebind timeout from 10s to 20s as a mitigation; that prevented some of these in staging. cost tradeoff: longer timeouts slightly increase slot hold time but reduce orphan churn.

ben_p: +1 on longer timeout as short-term fix. long-term we need stronger lease reconciliation so controllers proactively clear stale reservations on network hiccups.

carla: after descheduler dry-run: `Removed 32 orphaned leases, freed 28 slots` (03:18) — starting promoted run in 2m. :white_check_mark:

alice.m: promoted run done: `Freed 32 leases, 28 nodes now available, pending GPU pods started scheduling` — throughput normalizing.

sre-oncall: monitoring shows a 60% drop in pending pods and no further conntrack escalations after we rotated NAT gw.

ben_p: great. next steps: ticket to ops to look at NAT scaling + a short RFC for lease-controller reconciliation and a PR to bump latebind timeout to 20s. can we also add a metric for "sticky_lease_count"? that'll make incident detection easier.

dinesh: i'll own the RFC and metric. tagging @carla for rollout plan.

carla: will draft the rollout (canary on non-prod racks -> eu-west1 small rollout -> full). include a graceful backward-compatible flag for timeout.

alice.m: thanks team. leaving the thread here — will follow up in the RFC and ticket. :pray:
